title: 10. NLP, Transformers & LLMs: 5.1.1 Character Encoding
summary: Computers don't understand text—they only understand numbers (binary). Character encoding is the mapping between characters and numbers.
objectives: Learn the difference between ASCII, Unicode, and UTF-8
Identify and fix common encoding issues
Handle text data properly for NLP tasks

sections.title: The Fundamentals
sections.body:
### Why Character Encoding Matters

Computers don't understand text—they only understand numbers (binary). **Character encoding** is the mapping between characters and numbers.

```
Visual Representation:

Text (What you see)  →  Encoding  →  Binary (What computer stores)
     "Hello"         →   Mapping   →  01001000 01100101...
```

diagrams.title: From raw text to model input
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  raw["Raw text"] --> clean["Clean and normalise — unicode, case, HTML"]
  clean --> tok["Tokenise — words or subwords (BPE, WordPiece)"]
  tok --> ids["Map tokens to ids"]
  ids --> rep{"Representation"}
  rep --> bow["Sparse: bag of words, TF-IDF"]
  rep --> emb["Dense: word / sentence embeddings"]
  rep --> ctx["Contextual: transformer hidden states"]
diagrams.explain: Models never see text, only numbers. Text is normalised, split into tokens (subword tokenisers avoid out-of-vocabulary words), mapped to ids and then represented as sparse counts, static embeddings or contextual vectors from a transformer — each step a trade-off between simplicity and how much meaning is captured.

sections.title: 1 ASCII (American Standard Code for Information Interchange)
sections.body:
### Overview
- **Size**: 7 bits → 128 characters (0-127)
- **Coverage**: English letters, digits, punctuation, control characters
- **Created**: 1960s
- **Limitation**: Only supports English

### ASCII Table (Simplified)

```
┌─────────┬──────┬─────────┐
│ Decimal │ Char │  Binary │
├─────────┼──────┼─────────┤
│   65    │  A   │ 1000001 │
│   66    │  B   │ 1000010 │
│   97    │  a   │ 1100001 │
│   98    │  b   │ 1100010 │
│   48    │  0   │ 0110000 │
│   32    │ space│ 0100000 │
└─────────┴──────┴─────────┘
```

### ASCII Ranges

```
┌────────────────────────────────┐
│  0-31   : Control characters   │  (e.g., newline, tab)
│  32-47  : Symbols & punctuation│  (!, ", #, etc.)
│  48-57  : Digits 0-9           │
│  65-90  : Uppercase A-Z        │
│  97-122 : Lowercase a-z        │
│ 123-127 : More symbols         │
└────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Problem**: What about other languages? 你好 (Chinese), مرحبا (Arabic), हैलो (Hindi)?

sections.title: 2 Unicode
sections.body:
### The Solution to ASCII's Limitation

Unicode assigns a **unique number** (called a **code point**) to every character in every language.

```
Visual:

ASCII:     128 characters  [████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░]
Unicode: 149,186+ chars   [████████████████████████████████████]
                          (English, Chinese, Arabic, Emoji, etc.)
```

### Unicode Code Points

Format: `U+XXXX` (hexadecimal)

```
Examples:
┌──────────┬─────────────┬──────────┐
│   Char   │  Code Point │   Name   │
├──────────┼─────────────┼──────────┤
│    A     │   U+0041    │ Latin A  │
│    你    │   U+4F60    │ Chinese  │
│    😀    │   U+1F600   │ Emoji    │
│    🚀    │   U+1F680   │ Rocket   │
└──────────┴─────────────┴──────────┘
```

**Important**: Unicode is NOT an encoding—it's a **character set**. We need an encoding scheme to store Unicode characters.

sections.title: 3 UTF-8 (Unicode Transformation Format - 8 bit)
sections.body:
### Why UTF-8 is the Standard

UTF-8 is a **variable-length encoding** for Unicode:
- **Backward compatible** with ASCII
- **Space efficient** for English text
- **Universal** support for all languages

### How UTF-8 Works

```
Visual Encoding Rules:

1 byte  (ASCII):        0xxxxxxx                    (0-127)
2 bytes (Extended):     110xxxxx 10xxxxxx           (128-2047)
3 bytes (Most common):  1110xxxx 10xxxxxx 10xxxxxx  (2048-65535)
4 bytes (Emoji, etc.):  11110xxx 10xxxxxx 10xxxxxx 10xxxxxx
```

### UTF-8 Encoding Examples

#### Example 1: ASCII Character 'A'

```
Character: A
Code Point: U+0041 (65 in decimal)
Binary: 01000001

UTF-8 Encoding: 01000001 (1 byte)
                ^^^^^^^^
                Same as ASCII!
```

#### Example 2: Latin Character 'é'

```
Character: é
Code Point: U+00E9 (233 in decimal)
Binary: 11101001

UTF-8 Encoding: 11000011 10101001 (2 bytes)
                ^^          ^^^^
                Prefix      Data bits
```

#### Example 3: Chinese Character '你'

```
Character: 你
Code Point: U+4F60
Binary: 01001111 01100000

UTF-8 Encoding: 11100100 10111101 10100000 (3 bytes)
                ^^^^        ^^^^      ^^^^
                Prefix      Data      Data
```

#### Example 4: Emoji '😀'

```
Character: 😀
Code Point: U+1F600
Binary: 00011111 01100000 00000000

UTF-8 Encoding: 11110000 10011111 10011000 10000000 (4 bytes)
                ^^^^^^      ^^^^      ^^^^      ^^^^
                Prefix      Data      Data      Data
```

sections.title: Common Encoding Issues
sections.body:
### 1. Mojibake (文字化け)

**Problem**: Text displayed as gibberish when wrong encoding is used.

```python
# Example: UTF-8 bytes decoded as Latin-1
text = "café"
bytes_utf8 = text.encode('utf-8')      # b'caf\xc3\xa9'
wrong_decode = bytes_utf8.decode('latin-1')  # 'cafÃ©' ❌
correct_decode = bytes_utf8.decode('utf-8')  # 'café' ✓
```

**Visual**:
```
Expected: café
Mojibake: cafÃ©
```

### 2. Replacement Character �

**Problem**: Character can't be decoded—shows � (U+FFFD)

```python
# Invalid UTF-8 sequence
invalid_bytes = b'\xff\xfe'
try:
    text = invalid_bytes.decode('utf-8')
except UnicodeDecodeError:
    text = invalid_bytes.decode('utf-8', errors='replace')
    print(text)  # ��
```

### 3. Encoding/Decoding Errors

```
Common Error Flow:

UTF-8 file → Read as ASCII → ❌ UnicodeDecodeError
UTF-8 bytes → Decode as Latin-1 → Mojibake
Latin-1 text → Save as UTF-8 → ✓ Works, but may have issues later
```

sections.title: Practical Examples
sections.body:
### Example 1: Detecting Encoding

```python
# Check file encoding
import chardet

def detect_encoding(file_path):
    with open(file_path, 'rb') as f:
        raw_data = f.read()
        result = chardet.detect(raw_data)
        return result['encoding']

# Usage
encoding = detect_encoding('data.txt')
print(f"Detected encoding: {encoding}")
```

### Example 2: Proper File Reading

```python
# ✓ CORRECT: Specify encoding
with open('text.txt', 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    text = f.read()

# ❌ WRONG: Default encoding (system-dependent)
with open('text.txt', 'r') as f:  # Might fail on different systems
    text = f.read()
```

### Example 3: Handling Encoding Errors

```python
# Strategy 1: Replace invalid chars
with open('messy_file.txt', 'r', encoding='utf-8', errors='replace') as f:
    text = f.read()  # Invalid chars become �

# Strategy 2: Ignore invalid chars
with open('messy_file.txt', 'r', encoding='utf-8', errors='ignore') as f:
    text = f.read()  # Invalid chars removed

# Strategy 3: Strict (default) - raises error
try:
    with open('messy_file.txt', 'r', encoding='utf-8', errors='strict') as f:
        text = f.read()
except UnicodeDecodeError as e:
    print(f"Encoding error: {e}")
```

### Example 4: Converting Between Encodings

```python
# Convert file from Latin-1 to UTF-8
with open('old_file.txt', 'r', encoding='latin-1') as f_in:
    text = f_in.read()

with open('new_file.txt', 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f_out:
    f_out.write(text)
```

sections.title: Key Takeaways
sections.body:
### Encoding Hierarchy

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│         Character Set (Unicode)      │
│    "What characters exist?"          │
│    (Code points: U+0000 to U+10FFFF) │
└───────────────┬─────────────────────┘
                │
        ┌───────┴───────┐
        │   Encoding    │
        │ "How to store │
        │  in bytes?"   │
        └───────┬───────┘
                │
    ┌───────────┼───────────┐
    │           │           │
  UTF-8       UTF-16     UTF-32
(Variable)  (2 or 4)    (4 bytes)
```

### Best Practices

```
✓ DO:
  • Always use UTF-8 for new projects
  • Explicitly specify encoding when reading/writing files
  • Validate encoding of external data
  • Use .decode() and .encode() correctly

✗ DON'T:
  • Rely on default encoding
  • Mix encodings in the same project
  • Ignore encoding errors silently
  • Assume all text is ASCII
```
